title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Halloween (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted lift x2.65 from 3 past Halloween weeks; consistent with 2023-2025 data.

drivers.name: Store closed Monday
drivers.evidence: One-day closure likely reduces first-day sales; no data on partial-week impact, so conservative estimate.

drivers.name: Price increase (+6%)
drivers.evidence: Higher price may reduce demand slightly; no prior promotion at this price, so modest downside.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween drives a strong lift (x2.65 noise-adjusted), supported by 3 past occurrences. The price increase to $4.08 (+6%) is modest and likely outweighed by the holiday effect. Store closure on Monday reduces demand, but the holiday effect dominates. No prior promotion at this price level. The classical model’s x2.65 is well-supported by history. No overlap or double-counting. Downside risk is low due to strong historical consistency.

PRODUCT: Candy Corn Bag | category Candy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 (3 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat)
  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.3 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 24.2 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
